title: Area Model — Multiplication
prompt: Split 13 x 24 into its place-value parts and add them up.
learning_objective: Compute a two-digit product by decomposing the rectangle into partial products, and see that the total is the same however the rectangle is split.
reference: Area model of multiplication, as used in NRICH and Mathigon Polypad activities

spec.title: Area Model — 13 x 24
spec.instruction: The rectangle is 13 units wide and 24 units tall. Drag the dashed dividers to split it, then add the four sub-rectangles and enter the total area.

title: Area Model — Factoring
prompt: Build a rectangle with an area of 36 square units.
learning_objective: Find factor pairs of a whole number by building rectangles of a fixed area, and recognise that a number can have several factor pairs.
reference: Factors, multiples and divisibility; the area model used in reverse

spec.title: Area Model — Factor 36
spec.instruction: The target area is 36 square units. Drag the round side handles, or type the sides, until the rectangle has that area — then press Check.

title: Probability Lab — Biased Coin
concept: Experimental probability and the law of large numbers
prompt: Run trials and watch the observed proportion settle on the theoretical one.
learning_objective: Explain why the observed relative frequency approaches the theoretical probability as the number of trials grows, and predict that frequency for a fixed number of trials.
reference: Experimental probability and the law of large numbers

spec.title: Probability Lab — Biased Coin
spec.instruction: This coin comes up heads with probability 0.70. Run 1, 10, 100 and 1000 trials and watch the bars. Then predict the proportion of heads in a fresh run of 1000 trials.

title: Probability Lab — Fair Die
prompt: Roll a fair die many times and predict how often each face lands.
learning_objective: Compare an empirical distribution with a theoretical uniform distribution and predict the relative frequency of a single outcome after a fixed number of trials.
reference: Probability distributions; simulation and probability models

spec.title: Probability Lab — Fair Die
spec.instruction: A fair six-sided die: every face has probability 1/6. Run the trials and watch six bars, each with its own theoretical line. Then predict the proportion of 1s in a fresh run of 600 rolls.

title: Growing Pattern — Tiles
prompt: Extend the tile pattern, then state its rule.
learning_objective: Extend an arithmetic sequence by one term and describe it as t(n) = a + (n - 1)d, naming the first term and the common difference.

spec.title: Growing Pattern — Tiles
spec.instruction: Each row is one term of the pattern, one tile per unit. Work out the next term, then state the first term and the common difference.

title: Arithmetic Sequence — Find the Rule
prompt: Find the next term, then write the rule a + (n - 1)d.
learning_objective: Derive the first term and common difference of an arithmetic sequence from its terms and use them to write the general term.

spec.title: Arithmetic Sequence — Find the Rule
spec.instruction: The first five terms of an arithmetic sequence are shown. Give the sixth term, then state the first term and the common difference.

title: Step the Sort — Insertion Sort Comparisons
prompt: Step through insertion sort and predict its comparison count.
learning_objective: Trace insertion sort one comparison at a time and explain why its comparison count depends on the data rather than only on the array length.
reference: Comparison sorting algorithms; algorithm efficiency and Big-O

spec.title: Insertion Sort — Count the Comparisons
spec.instruction: Step forward and back through the sort. The Comparisons chip counts every pair the algorithm looks at. Then predict the total.

title: Step the Sort — Bubble Sort State
prompt: Step through bubble sort and predict the array part-way through.
learning_objective: Trace bubble sort one comparison and swap at a time and predict the state of the array after a given number of steps.

spec.title: Bubble Sort — State After Five Steps
spec.instruction: Each step is one comparison; a swap moves the two highlighted bars. Step through, then predict the array after 5 steps.
